An estimated 50,000 to 60,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Spain's Ceuta by land and sea in an unprecedented two-day surge. At least 57 people died during the crossings.   By Friday evening, Spanish authorities said about 48,300 had returned to Morocco. According to media reports, many were drawn by false online claims that Spain would provide shelter, visas or a route to the mainland, only to find reception facilities overwhelmed and no way to continue their journey.   Spain deployed troops and tightened border controls, while Moroccan police resumed intercepting people attempting new crossings. The surge has highlighted both humanitarian and political challenges at Europe's southern border.  #Ceuta #MigrationCrisis #Morocco #Spain #WorldNews

my grandfather has owned this whole land, house and all the fruit it bore since the 70s, my mother, all her siblings and all their children grew up there. it was a home but also the family business. generations of moroccans are being put out on the street without proper compensation, not just us but everywhere in rabat. my grandparents are old, you can see how much love is in every worn out chair, hand-made mosaic tiles or plant cared for by my grandmother. it breaks my heart to see my family loose their existential grounds & nobody knowing what to do with themselves. they’ve tried laywers and all but you can only do so much against a royal order. the worst part is the land in front of us was already taken & evacuated & instead of actual state projects, there’s a private villa by a khaleeji man now. to take away decades old homes from moroccans for cheap and give them to rich khaleejis is a form of violence that de-roots you so deeply. they gave us 10 days before they send special forces. #morocco #rabat #saverabat  #landgrab #anticapitalism

Would you wander Marrakech alone?  One thing I was honestly nervous about before coming to Marrakech for the first time was safety, especially as a woman travelling alone. Social media can make the medina look super intimidating, chaotic, and overwhelming, but my experience has actually been really positive. Of course you need to stay aware like in any big city, but I’ve spent hours wandering the souks, getting lost in little alleyways, shopping, stopping for mint tea, and exploring on my own and I genuinely felt okay. One thing that helped SO much this time was not carrying all my luggage around with me 😅 dragging a huge backpack through crowded streets instantly makes you feel more stressed and overwhelmed. I used @bounce luggage storage so I could explore Marrakech freely for the day before my riad check-in, and it made such a difference. I could actually enjoy the medina instead of worrying about my bags the entire time. Bounce has thousands of locations worldwide and is a super reliable resource if you find yourself in a similar situation as me. If you’re travelling soon, you can use my code SARAHBOUNCE for a discount! #travelhacks #travelreccommendations #solotraveller
